A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA-RITE research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning accuracy, generation scores, training throughput, rank ablations and factor-norm measurements, including Gemma2-2B results in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and throughput results and reports additional training-loss curves, relative-update measurements and rank-ablation results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces QR decomposition with polar decomposition, ordinary inverses with pseudoinverses, and introduces division by m in the second-moment contribution. These refine the retained optimizer. The scaling change appears in the pseudocode but not the corresponding moment equation; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Super-Natural Instructions, HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge, GSM8K and OpenBookQA. The additional rank studies and diagnostics retain these tasks; removing Gemma2-2B changes model configurations, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their comparator memberships. Locally, the new factor-update diagnostics in Figures 3–4 compare LoRA-RITE with Adam, LoRA+, ScaledAdam and Shampoo, extending the diagnostic comparison beyond the three baselines plotted in v1's retained factor-norm Figure 1.

E3.justification: The original splits, training budgets and benchmark metrics remain unchanged. v2 adds rank-64 evaluation, extends rank-4 evaluation across the four LLM benchmarks, and adds training-loss and relative-update measurements. The Gemma2-2B evaluation configuration is removed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained OpenBookQA rank/architecture ablation and Figure 1, v2 adds training-loss comparisons, normalized factor-update diagnostics on two datasets, and rank-4/16/64 sensitivity across four benchmarks (Appendices A.7–A.9). These substantially expand analysis of optimization behavior and rank dependence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or statistical significance tests. The added plots do not introduce uncertainty bands.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results, but the supplementary evidence changes substantially. v1's Gemma2-2B results disappear, including average scores of 77.75 for LoRA-RITE and 77.27 for Adam. v2 adds rank-dependent scores, including rank-64 Gemma-2B averages of 59.52 and 56.08 respectively, plus loss/update trajectories. These are different configurations and newly reported outcomes, not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Definition 1 changes from arbitrary equal-product factorizations to pairs related by an invertible transformation. Section 3.1 revises the diagonal-preconditioning argument. Assumption 1 gains a trace condition, and the convergence proofs incorporate escaped mass, including a new bound in Lemma 3. These substantively revise the mathematical foundations despite retaining the headline convergence rates.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same headline claims: transformation-invariant adaptive LoRA optimization, convergence analysis, low overhead and improved benchmark performance. The added analyses do not introduce a new principal contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits applicability to objectives of the form f(AB^T) and adds explanations of rank effects through regularization and approaching full fine-tuning. It removes v1's explanation for the small Gemma2 gains. These are localized qualifications and interpretations; the principal factor-balancing explanation remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides a project-code access statement and repository link, while Appendix A.10/Table 9 discloses the best learning rate for each optimizer and benchmark on Gemma-2B. The general hyperparameter table and TPU information are retained. The new learning-rate disclosure does not establish a changed tuning procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al. (2022), Revisiting Parameter-Efficient Tuning: Are We Really There Yet?, to support the regularization discussion. The related-work positioning is otherwise retained; consolidating the duplicate Lamb references is bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: The invariance explanations and appendix proofs receive localized rewrites and clearer cross-references. v2 separates the Theorem 4 proof into its own subsection, adds acknowledgments and conference headers, and compacts the author block. The main section order and most narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds three two-panel diagnostic figures and rank-ablation and learning-rate tables, while removing the Gemma2 table. Figure 1 is relocated before Section 3 and its captions are revised. This substantially expands the visual presentation, although the retained benchmark tables keep essentially the same structure.

improvement.justification: The broader rank study, loss/update diagnostics and selected learning rates make the optimizer's behavior easier to assess and reproduce. Explicit additional assumptions and applicability limits better qualify its guarantees. These gains are tempered by removing the informative small-gain Gemma2 results, the normalization inconsistency between Algorithm 1 and its equation, and an untested interpretation involving full fine-tuning. Overall, the improvement is useful but limited.
